title: The United States Loses Its Measles Elimination Status After a Year of Spread
title_zh: 美国失去麻疹消除认证：疫情持续传播已超过一年
source_name: KFF Health News — “US Has Lost Measles Elimination Status, Global Health Authorities Say” (14 Nov 2026)
summary_zh: 据KFF健康新闻11月14日报道，熟悉审议情况的研究人员表示，泛美卫生组织（PAHO，与世界卫生组织合作负责美洲卫生事务）已于本周认定美国失去麻疹消除认证；原计划于11月17日正式对外公布。美国曾在2000年实现这一目标。按照公共卫生标准，“消除”允许偶发疫情，但疫情须在一年内结束；如今病毒已连续传播超过12个月。约翰斯·霍普金斯大学估计，过去两年已有8000多人患病、830多人住院，并造成约1.25亿美元的医疗、防疫和生产力损失；各州报告13例相关死亡，其中包括尚不能接种疫苗的婴儿。两剂麻疹-腮腺炎-风疹疫苗可预防约97%的感染，社区接种率达到95%才能形成群体免疫；自2025年1月以来的7600多例确诊中，仅3%发生在已接种者身上。美洲地区已因加拿大在2025年出现地方性传播而失去无麻疹状态。美国要恢复认证，须先遏制当前疫情，并确保今后疫情不超过一年。
paragraphs: This week, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) concluded that the United States has lost its measles elimination status, a public-health achievement first reached in 2000. PAHO works with the World Health Organization on health across the Americas. Researchers familiar with the decision said a public announcement had been planned for 17 November. In official language, "elimination" means that occasional outbreaks in a country still end within a year. That is no longer happening in the United States.

The finding follows the country's worst measles resurgence in decades. Johns Hopkins University researchers estimate that more than 8,000 people have been sickened in the past two years. More than 830 have been admitted to hospital, and the outbreaks have cost about 125 million dollars in medical care, public-health work and lost productivity. States have reported 13 measles-associated deaths, including several infants. Babies in the United States are usually not given the measles vaccine before their first birthday, so the youngest children depend on protection around them.

Measles is highly contagious, but outbreaks are almost entirely preventable. Two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine prevent about 97 per cent of infections. When at least 95 per cent of people in a community are immunized, so-called herd immunity also protects those who cannot be vaccinated, such as young infants. After elimination, most later U.S. outbreaks began with the virus brought from abroad and then faded. Now vaccination gaps have allowed the same strain to keep spreading for more than 12 months — the official test for re-established transmission.

Childhood vaccination rates have declined since the COVID-19 pandemic, and many recent infections have been concentrated in communities with low coverage. Of more than 7,600 confirmed cases since January 2025, only 3 per cent were in people who had been vaccinated. The virus can cause a high fever and missed days of school or work, and in serious cases it can lead to blindness, deafness, brain damage or death.

The Americas already lost its measles-free status in 2025, after endemic transmission — meaning the virus kept circulating locally — returned in Canada. To regain the status, the United States must stop the current outbreaks and then keep future ones from lasting a full year. Experts warn this may not happen soon, because outbreaks are still growing in several states.
paragraphs_zh: 本周，泛美卫生组织（PAHO）认定，美国已失去麻疹消除认证。这一公共卫生成就最初是在2000年取得的。泛美卫生组织与世界卫生组织合作，负责美洲地区的卫生事务。熟悉该决定的研究人员表示，原计划于11月17日公开发布这一结论。用官方术语来说，“消除”是指一个国家里偶发的疫情仍会在一年内结束。如今，美国的情况已不再如此。
这一结论出现在该国数十年来最严重的麻疹再度流行之后。约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的研究人员估计，过去两年已有8000多人患病。住院人数超过830人，这些疫情在医疗、公共卫生工作和生产力损失方面造成了约1.25亿美元的代价。各州已报告13例与麻疹相关的死亡，其中包括数名婴儿。在美国，婴儿通常要到一周岁以后才会接种麻疹疫苗，因此最小的孩子要依靠周围人的保护。
麻疹的传染性很强，但疫情几乎完全可以预防。两剂麻疹-腮腺炎-风疹疫苗可预防约97%的感染。当一个社区中至少95%的人已获得免疫时，所谓的“群体免疫”也能保护那些无法接种疫苗的人，例如幼婴。在实现消除之后，美国后来的多数疫情始于病毒从国外传入，随后逐渐平息。如今，疫苗接种缺口已使同一毒株持续传播超过12个月——这正是判定传播已再度确立的官方标准。
自新冠疫情以来，儿童疫苗接种率有所下降，近期许多感染集中出现在覆盖率较低的社区。自2025年1月以来确诊的7600多例病例中，只有3%发生在已接种疫苗的人身上。这种病毒可引起高烧，并导致缺课或误工；严重时，还可能导致失明、失聪、脑损伤或死亡。
美洲地区已在2025年失去了无麻疹状态，此前加拿大出现了地方性传播——也就是病毒在当地持续循环。要重新获得这一认证，美国必须先遏制当前的疫情，然后确保今后的疫情不会持续整整一年。专家警告说，这可能不会很快实现，因为疫情仍在多个州扩大。

phrases.meaning_zh: 偶发疫情；偶尔出现的暴发
再度确立的传播（疾病重新在本地持续传播）

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A new measles vaccine invented by Johns Hopkins University.
The United States losing its measles elimination status after the virus spread for more than a year.
A decision by Canada to ban measles vaccination.
A plan by PAHO to wipe out measles worldwide by 17 November.
questions.explanation: 全文主旨是泛美卫生组织认定美国失去麻疹消除认证，因为病毒已持续传播超过一年；并解释疫苗保护、病例数据和恢复认证的条件。文中并未说约翰斯·霍普金斯大学发明了新疫苗，也未提到加拿大禁止接种，或PAHO计划在11月17日前在全球消灭麻疹。

evidence.quote: the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) concluded that the United States has lost its measles elimination status

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how effective are two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine?
options: They prevent about 3 per cent of infections.
They must be given only after a person is already sick.
They prevent about 97 per cent of infections.
They protect only infants under one year old.
questions.explanation: 第三段明确写道，两剂麻疹-腮腺炎-风疹疫苗可预防约97%的感染。3%指的是自2025年1月以来确诊病例中已接种者所占的比例，不是疫苗有效率；疫苗也不是患病后才接种，而且一岁以下婴儿通常还不能接种，需要依靠群体免疫来保护。

evidence.quote: Two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine prevent about 97 per cent of infections.

questions.prompt: Why are young infants at special risk during these outbreaks?
options: Because measles vaccines are more dangerous for babies than the disease itself.
Because PAHO has banned infant vaccination in the United States.
Because measles only affects children under one year old.
Because they are usually not vaccinated before their first birthday and depend on protection around them.
questions.explanation: 第二段说明，美国婴儿通常要到一周岁以后才接种麻疹疫苗，因此最小的孩子要依靠周围人的保护；第三段也指出群体免疫可以保护无法接种的幼婴。由此可以推断，幼婴在疫情中特别危险，是因为他们往往还不能接种，必须依赖周围已免疫的人。文中并未说疫苗比疾病更危险、PAHO禁止给婴儿接种，或麻疹只影响一岁以下儿童。

evidence.quote: Babies in the United States are usually not given the measles vaccine before their first birthday, so the youngest children depend on protection around them.
